categories.main_business_segments: IHI Corporation operates four main business segments: Resources, Energy & Environment (including engines, carbon solutions, and nuclear equipment), Social Infrastructure (bridges, water gates, transportation systems, and urban development), Industrial Systems & General-Purpose Machinery (turbochargers, parking systems, rotating machinery, logistics/industrial systems), and Aerospace & Defense (aircraft engines, rocket systems, and defense equipment).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: IHI leverages advanced engineering and manufacturing technologies such as combustion and propulsion systems for engines, ammonia combustion for clean energy, precision machining for turbochargers, AI-driven infrastructure diagnostics, and digital transformation (DX) for production efficiency. The company also focuses on lifecycle business models and value chain integration, with significant R&D in electrification, hydrogen propulsion, and sustainable aviation fuels.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include airlines (notably via the Japan Aero Engines Association), governments and public sector entities (for infrastructure and defense), automotive manufacturers (for turbochargers), industrial companies, and energy utilities. Major end markets are aerospace, defense, energy, transportation, logistics, and public infrastructure sectors.
categories.geographic_coverage: IHI operates globally with significant business in Japan, North America, Asia (notably China, Southeast Asia, and India), and Europe. The company has manufacturing, engineering, and sales subsidiaries in the US, China, Southeast Asia, Europe, and other regions, with a strong export and overseas project portfolio.
categories.supply_chain_position: IHI is primarily positioned as a midstream to downstream manufacturer and systems integrator, providing finished products, large-scale systems, and engineering solutions directly to end-users and governments, while also engaging in upstream activities such as component manufacturing and technology development.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include accelerating growth in aerospace (especially aircraft engines and rockets), expanding clean energy solutions (notably ammonia and hydrogen value chains), and transforming core businesses for higher efficiency and sustainability. R&D focuses on carbon neutrality, electrification, digital transformation, AI/automation, and advanced materials, with a strong ESG (environmental, social, governance) orientation.
categories.revenue_model: IHI generates revenue primarily through product sales (engines, machinery, infrastructure systems), engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contracts, lifecycle services (maintenance, repair, and overhaul), and leasing/real estate income. The company also receives government grants and subsidies for R&D and innovation projects.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include global engineering and heavy industry firms such as Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Kawasaki Heavy Industries, and Hitachi, as well as international aerospace and energy companies. IHI is positioned as a leading Japanese diversified engineering group with strong capabilities in aerospace, energy, and infrastructure, often competing on technology, reliability, and lifecycle solutions.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In FY2024 (ending March 2025), IHI reported consolidated revenue of ¥1,626.8 billion (approx. $10.5 billion), operating profit of ¥143.5 billion, and net profit attributable to owners of ¥112.7 billion. The company experienced a strong rebound in profitability and revenue, driven by aerospace and energy segments, with a workforce of approximately 28,000 employees and a global asset base exceeding ¥2.2 trillion.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: IHI emphasizes its ability to deliver advanced, reliable, and sustainable engineering solutions that address critical social challenges such as decarbonization, infrastructure resilience, and mobility. The company differentiates through deep technical expertise, integrated lifecycle services, global project execution, and a strong commitment to ESG and innovation in clean energy and aerospace.
